notes.lines: Every precinct, county, legislative, congressional and State Board of Education line, and every judicial circuit's, is a 2020 census block's, generalised by at most 1.5 metres and set on a grid of 0.00001 degree (about a metre). A point within a few metres of a line can fall on either side of it.
notes.precincts: Alabama publishes no statewide map of its precincts as they stand in 2026. Each shape here is a voting district as the county reported it for the 2020 census, cut wherever a House, Senate, congressional or State Board of Education line crosses it, and named as the Census Bureau's file names it (Alabama's precincts are mostly named for their voting place). A county may have redrawn, renamed or moved its precincts since: the county's board of registrars and probate judge are the authority. What a ballot depends on (county, legislative, congressional and Board of Education district, judicial circuit, city or town, school system) is taken from current files and does not depend on the precinct.
notes.legislative: Which House and Senate district a block is in is the Census Bureau's 2024 equivalency file's word: the plans the Legislature enacted in 2021. The Senate plan is the one in force for 2026: a federal court's remedial plan for the Montgomery districts (25 and 26) was stayed by the Eleventh Circuit on May 28, 2026.
notes.congressional: The congressional districts are the Legislature's 2023 plan (Act 2023-563), in force for 2026 after the U.S. Supreme Court's order of June 2, 2026; the lines differ from 2024's. Each block is put in the district the Legislature's own layer gives it, and the 2020 population of every district so put together equals the plan's own figure, so a precinct's district is exact.
notes.board_of_education: The State Board of Education districts (the 2021 plan) are put together and checked the same way; sboe is a precinct property and has no layer, since every Board seat is drawn on the ballot pages as the state.
notes.judicial: The 41 judicial circuits are whole counties (Code of Alabama 12-11-2); a circuit judge is elected by the whole circuit. A district court judge is elected by the whole county.
notes.places: Cities and towns are the Census Bureau's 2025 places. A precinct lying wholly in one names it (mcd); one that reaches into cities or towns lists them (mcd_all, with each one's share of the precinct's area), and a precinct partly outside every city names no place of its own: the mcd layer answers for a point. Alabama's cities and towns hold their elections in August, not on November 3, so no city or town contest is on this ballot.
notes.commissioners: Most county commissions in Alabama are elected by district, and each county keeps its own lines. Only Jefferson County's (the Board of Registrars', effective November 4, 2021) and Baldwin County's (the County Commission's) are published for scripts, and only those are drawn (the com layer; a precinct's com is the district holding most of it, analysis, and the layer answers for a point). Every other county's commission contests are listed under check, with the reason.
notes.school: School system lines are the Census Bureau's 2025 file of the systems' own boundaries. A county system is the county less its city systems; which voters elect a county board of education is set by local law and differs from county to county, so the county's sample ballot is the authority. Which systems a precinct lies in is analysis, not an official list: a system counts when its piece of the precinct is at least 60 metres thick somewhere; school_pct is each system's share of the precinct's area (land and water, not voters).
notes.authority: For which precinct an address votes in, and where, the county's board of registrars and probate judge and the Secretary of State's Alabama Votes lookup are the authority.
notes.precinct_ids: A precinct's id is its county's five digits, a full stop and the Census Bureau's 2020 voting district code (01073.000123); a voting district cut by a district line has .p and the piece's number after it (01011.0012-1.p2); the Bureau's own codes can hold a full stop or a hyphen (0012.2, 0002-1).
